body:
Burn-down complete (--status approved). 4 specs shipped, 0 parked mid-flight, main verified green.

Completed:
- BUG-774 queue add --for <role> invisible to other users -> https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1580
- BUG-775 queue done accepts a spec whose latest review verdict is RequestChanges -> https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1581
- BUG-776 session end auto-files an empty Review PR-0 story on remote-less repos -> https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1578
- BUG-777 orphaned leases block queue work with no self-service recovery -> https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1579
All four auto-bumped to Completed on pull. main is at 39490ce53.

Caveats / verifications worth noting:
- The integrated-main check was stronger than the usual compile-only gate, deliberately: BUG-774/775 both landed in queue code and BUG-776/777 both in session code, so each pair could have broken together despite four separate greens. Ran cargo build -p aida-cli plus env -u AIDA_SESSION_ROLE cargo test -p aida-cli-lib -p aida-core on the union: 832 passed, 0 failed, and cargo fmt --all --check clean.
- BUG-775 shipped a SAFETY GATE (refuse queue done when the latest verdict is RequestChanges and the branch tip has not advanced past the reviewed sha, plus a commits-ahead check that now resolves against a LOCAL default branch instead of silently no-opping without an origin remote). It has tests, but it is gate logic that changes refusal behavior on a hot path and it merged without human review. Worth your eyes before it is relied on.
- I scoped the four implementers with explicit ownership fences (774=queue read path, 775=queue done gate, 776=session-end auto-file, 777=lease claim) precisely because 776 and 777 both touch session end. No merge conflicts resulted.

Disposed without implementing (2 of the 6 blessed specs):
- TASK-1016 DEFERRED, not implemented. It flips the solo-loop DEFAULT groom step to --autopilot, i.e. it changes the autonomy machinery itself, and its own title names the precondition "once the envelope is proven in supervised use". Shipping that through an unattended drain would violate the burndown guardrail AND short-circuit the specs own precondition. Revisit trigger recorded against TASK-0429. It wants a keyboard session.
- TASK-1135 CLOSED as already-delivered, verified against code not docs: handle_auto_complete_single_branch at aida-cli-lib/src/queue_cmd.rs:4647, dispatched at :4633, landed under TASK-1003 / SPIKE-70. I also closed its sibling TASK-1134 on the same evidence (cli.rs:4960 single_branch, :4973 --sequential with conflicts_with, test at cli.rs:11960).

NEEDS YOUR DECISION - a filing-quality problem, not a code problem:
TASK-1134/1135/1136/1137 were all filed as STORY-711 followups with titles truncated mid-sentence and EMPTY descriptions. Two of them (1134, 1135) were already implemented and still sat Approved; 1135 was blessed onto the queue and reached my ready set, where a less careful runner would have re-implemented shipped work. TASK-1136 (cluster PR) and TASK-1137 (per-member checkpoint hook) are still Approved with the same malformed shape and are likely OBE too - TASK-1136 in particular looks covered by the cluster-PR work in digest.rs (see the collapse_cluster_pr_models_single_branch_cluster test). They are awaiting_signoff so I did not touch them. Recommend you sweep that family. The deeper issue: the burndown gate cannot detect an unimplementable or already-done filing, so followup auto-filing that truncates titles and drops descriptions is feeding junk into the drain.

Left for manual merge: none.

Worktrees not pruned: my four were pruned cleanly (worktrees, local branches, remote branches). Three PRE-EXISTING agent worktrees from an earlier session remain at .claude/worktrees/agent-{a942df7439695a8aa,ab76dad2f2712ef43,ada058a96e1aba25f}, all stuck at d9f9eceb8, plus 9 worktree-agent-* branches still on origin. Not from this drain, so I left them; they are accumulating.

Parked by the gate (unchanged, no action taken): TASK-735, TASK-751 (deferred:on-demand), TASK-749 (deferred:future-rbac), TASK-892 (deferred:until-projects-toml-consumed), STORY-687, STORY-688 (deferred:cockpit-phase2), EPIC-44 (epic, needs decomposition).
